situation:
You are a second-year electrician apprentice, earning while you train, and you rent a studio across town from most of your job sites. A financial coach (judge) at CEDARWORKS FINANCIAL COACHING meets with apprentices for free, and you have booked a session to talk through buying a used truck.

You have $4,200 saved and no credit history at all. A private seller will take the $4,200 in cash for a high-mileage pickup, which empties the savings and still leaves a lender nothing to read about you. BRIGHTWAY MOTORS will finance a certified pickup over thirty-six months for $1,340 in interest.

Those payments, made on time, would build the credit history a mortgage lender reads years from now, but the first one falls in the same month your lease term ends and the landlord renews at $1,150 with an added security deposit. The dealership's account posts daily countdown videos on a payment-only offer that expires Sunday.

You could also keep riding to job sites with a coworker for another year and save toward a down payment, though you would depend on his schedule and stay a renter longer. The coach (judge) wants you to compare the paths and recommend one. The coach (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a financial coach (judge) at CEDARWORKS FINANCIAL COACHING. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You sit with apprentices and first-time borrowers who are deciding what to do with the first real savings they have ever held. You want to hear the paths compared and hear which one this apprentice would take, along with what it does to the money left over each month.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Which choice did you leave on the table, and what would it have given you?
What would you have given up to take it instead?
